note: Adapted from the redescription by Onagbola & Scheffrahn (2017) (in English), which gives prose descriptions and measurement tables for both the alate and the soldier; the soldier is described here for the first time (the original reads 'first description of the N. agilis soldier'). The original description is Sjöstedt 1904 (Calotermes agilis). The authors note that in this species the alate fore wing has the radius sector and media fused into a single vein, unique within Neotermes. In the OCR of the measurement tables many of the max/min/mean triplets retain only one column, so only legible values are recorded.

sections.label: Alate
sections.text: A small species. Vertex and frons reddish brown, gradually becoming pale reddish brown behind, paler near the anteclypeal suture. Pronotum concolorous with the dorsum of the head, only the anterior third with a pale area; anteclypeus yellow, labrum concolorous with the genae. Abdominal tergites yellowish brown, sternites pale yellow to transparent. Coxae and femora pale yellow, femora and tarsi pale brown. Meso- and metanota concolorous with the vertex, the overlapping wing scales forming a V-shaped mark on the pronotum. Compound eyes grey-black; ocelli and the antennal segments concolorous with the labrum. Sides of the head slightly converging in dorsal view; cranial suture fine and clear. Vertex smooth, frons slightly concave. Compound eyes large, slightly convex and nearly circular; ocelli very large and ellipsoidal, touching the compound eyes. Antennae 14—16-segmented. Pronotum nearly flat in dorsal view. Fore wing venation unique in the genus: the main veins sclerotized only at the base, the radius sector and media fused into a single vein; the radius sector and media paler in colour, brown only at the base. Left mandible with 3 marginal teeth; right mandible with 2 large subapical teeth. Pronotum as wide as the head, anterior margin shallowly concave, anterolateral angles rounded (about 70°), sides parallel, posterior margin straight in the middle.

sections.label: Soldier
sections.text: Monomorphic. In dorsal view the head capsule is deep reddish brown at the antennae, becoming pale yellow-orange towards the back of the head; mandibles black. The basal 3 antennal segments reddish brown, the distal segments gradually paler. Eye spot pale yellowish brown and elongate, smaller than the antennal fossa. Margin of the pronotum yellow-orange-brown; postmentum chestnut; labrum concolorous with the vertex. In dorsal view the head capsule is narrowly rectangular, the sides slightly concave and slightly narrowing anteriorly; the posterior angles evenly rounded; the posterior margin straight. In lateral and oblique view the head capsule is almost cylindrical, only slightly compressed dorsoventrally. In dorsal view the frontal margin forms a right angle of 60°, producing a deep notch; in lateral or oblique view the anterolateral angle of the frontal margin bears a small tubercle. Vertex with lateral grooves, the sides with distinct ridges. Frons sloping about 40° from the vertex; mandibles curved upwards about 20°. Hairs of the frons and vertex very short and sparse. Circumantennal ridge well developed; mandibles stout, about half the length of the head capsule; tooth pattern clear, the left mandible with 3 submarginal teeth, the two proximal ones separated by a shallow notch; the proximal tooth of the right mandible hidden by the labrum; apical tooth about 70°; basal tubercle moderate and wrinkled. Labrum ligulate and medium-sized, with long apical bristles. Antennae 12-segmented, segment 3 slightly enlarged but shorter than the sum of segments 4 and 5. Pronotum wider than the head, shield-shaped, the anterior margin evenly concave, the anterolateral angles about 60° and acute, the sides converging posteriorly, the posterior margin forming an even shallow convexity. All femora swollen. Fore femur swollen.

sections.label: Other
sections.text: Alate measurements (n=10, mm; maximum/minimum/mean): head length including labrum 1.54; head length to the postclypeus 1.28; greatest head width at the compound eyes 1.40/1.28/1.33; head height (without postmentum) 0.84; greatest labrum width 0.50; compound eye diameter (including the sclerite) 0.49; least distance from the compound eye to the base of the head 0.16; greatest ocellus diameter 0.19, least diameter 0.14; greatest pronotum length 0.72, greatest width 1.41; body length including wings 11.16; body length without wings 5.98; fore wing length from the wing suture 8.90; greatest fore wing width 2.24; hind tibia length 0.94; antennal segment count 15. Soldier measurements (n=2): head length to the tip of the mandibles 3.20; head length to the postclypeus 2.20/2.20/2.20; greatest head width 1.55/1.50/1.53; distance between the frontal processes 0.95/0.80/0.88; head height (without postmentum) 1.25; greatest labrum width 0.38/0.25/0.31; greatest postclypeus width 0.43/0.40/0.41; left mandible length (tip to the farthest point of the ventral condyle) 1.25/1.20/1.23; length of the middle of the postmentum 1.28; greatest postmentum width 0.58/0.48/0.55; least postmentum width 0.18/0.15/0.16; greatest pronotum width 1.50/1.45/1.48, greatest length 0.95/0.85/0.90; hind tibia length 0.83; body length 7.62/7.70; antennae 12-segmented. Material examined: Bobiri Butterfly Sanctuary, Ghana (6.690, −1.338), 12 September (month 9) 2006, collected by L. R. Davis (UF number AFR188), 2 soldiers and 16 alates and nymphs, from a piece of hardwood.
